body.statement: Under the same one-observation law with \(p_n=p\) fixed before \(n\to\infty\), the true-propensity IPW and oracle DR bulk-coordinate gradient variances at \(\beta=0\) are \(1/8\) and \(v_\gamma/4\), respectively. On \(\mathcal E_{0n}\cap\mathcal E_{1n}\cap\mathcal Q_n\), the exact linear entropy-balance variance is \(1/16\); this event has probability tending to one in the fixed-dimensional limit. Consequently, as \(\kappa\downarrow0\) after the proportional limits, \(r_T=\kappa/(4\lambda)+o(\kappa)\), \(r_E=\kappa/(8\lambda)+o(\kappa)\), and \(r_D=v_\gamma\kappa/(2\lambda)+o(\kappa)\), provided the certified-event uniform remainder asserted by the joint system holds. The uniform complement-event fallback is not identified with entropy balancing in this reduction.
body.justification: This sanity reduction anchors the proportional system to the classical HIR projection while showing that linear balance remains strictly short of oracle DR when \(\gamma>0\).
body.gap: HiranoImbensRidder2003 and FangRidderXie2026 obtain full efficiency from sufficiently rich estimated propensity scores; the exact same-coordinate linear balance used here spans only a partial projection.
body.consumer: The reduction gives analysts a low-dimensional diagnostic and prevents interpreting exact linear balance as automatic oracle efficiency.
body.proof_tex:
Fix an integer \(p\) before taking \(n\to\infty\), and fix a bulk coordinate \(k\in\{2,\ldots,p\}\).  By Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}fixed\mbox{-}dimensional\mbox{-}score\mbox{-}projection}\), under Assumptions \(\mathrm{ass{:}gaussian\mbox{-}features}\), \(\mathrm{ass{:}randomization}\), and \(\mathrm{ass{:}binary\mbox{-}logistic\mbox{-}outcome}\), the one-observation gradient influences at the origin are
\[
 \psi_{T,k}=\frac12 S Yq_k,
 \qquad
 \psi_{E,k}=\frac12 S\left[\left(Y-\frac12\right)q_k-\mu_k\right],
 \qquad
 \psi_{D,k}=\frac12 S\{Y-m(q)\}q_k,
\]
where \(\mu=\mathbb E\{m(q)q\}\) and \(\mu_k=0\) for \(k>1\).  The same lemma proves
\[
 s_T:=\operatorname{Var}(\psi_{T,k})=\frac18,
 \qquad
 s_E:=\operatorname{Var}(\psi_{E,k})=\frac1{16},
 \qquad
 s_D:=\operatorname{Var}(\psi_{D,k})=\frac{v_\gamma}{4}.
\]
It also proves, in this fixed-dimensional regime,
\[
 \mathbb P(\mathcal E_{0n}\cap\mathcal E_{1n}\cap\mathcal Q_n)\longrightarrow1.
\]
Therefore the displayed method-\(E\) influence and variance concern the unique exact-balancing weights supplied by Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}entropy\mbox{-}weights}\) on the certified event.  They use no entropy-balancing property of the uniform complement-event convention.

We next derive the curvature that converts these score variances into the claimed small-aspect regret coefficients.  From the definitions of \(\sigma\) and \(h\), direct differentiation gives
\[
 \sigma'(0)=\frac14,
 \qquad
 \sigma''(0)=0,
 \qquad
 h'(z)=z\sigma'(z),
 \qquad
 h''(0)=\frac14.
\]
Let \(G_{jn}=\nabla F_{jn}(0)\).  Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}empirical\mbox{-}objectives}\) then yields, for each \(j\in\mathcal J\),
\[
 \nabla^2F_{jn}(0)
 =\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n
 \left\{c_{j,ni}\sigma''(0)-\lambda h''(0)\right\}q_{ni}q_{ni}^{\top}
 =-\frac{\lambda}{4}\frac{Q_n^{\top}Q_n}{n}.
\]
For fixed \(p\), Assumption \(\mathrm{ass{:}gaussian\mbox{-}features}\) gives, for every pair of coordinates \((k,\ell)\),
\[
 \mathbb E(q_{ni,k}q_{ni,\ell})=\mathbf 1\{k=\ell\},
 \qquad
 \operatorname{Var}(q_{ni,k}q_{ni,\ell})<\infty.
\]
Chebyshev's inequality and a union bound over the fixed set of \(p^2\) coordinate pairs consequently imply
\[
 \frac{Q_n^{\top}Q_n}{n}\longrightarrow_{\mathbb P}I_p,
 \qquad
 \nabla^2F_{jn}(0)\longrightarrow_{\mathbb P}-\frac{\lambda}{4}I_p.
\]
The inverse local curvature is therefore \(4/\lambda\), which is well defined because \(\lambda>0\).

The rate conclusion in the proposition is expressly conditional on the certified-event uniform remainder furnished by an affirmative resolution of \(\mathrm{oeq{:}joint\mbox{-}phase\mbox{-}system}\).  We now make explicit the two consequences of that stated proviso used below.  After first taking the proportional limit \(p_n/n\to\kappa\) on \(\mathcal E_{0n}\cap\mathcal E_{1n}\cap\mathcal Q_n\), and then taking \(\kappa\downarrow0\), it permits the fixed-coordinate score calculation to be aggregated over the \(p_n-1\) bulk coordinates and makes the local quadratic expansion uniform at the selected global maximizer.  Equivalently, for every \(j\in\mathcal J\), it gives
\[
 \|G_{jn}\|_2^2=s_j\frac{p_n}{n}+o_{\mathbb P}(\kappa)
 =s_j\kappa+o_{\mathbb P}(\kappa)
\]
and
\[
 \left\|\widehat\beta_{jn}-\frac4\lambda G_{jn}\right\|_2
 =o_{\mathbb P}(\sqrt\kappa).
\]
The first relation uses the three variances already proved above.  The only exceptional coordinate is the signal coordinate \(1\); the same uniform remainder controls its squared score by \(O_{\mathbb P}(n^{-1})\), which vanishes before the subsequent \(\kappa\downarrow0\) limit.  The second relation is the score equation linearized using the nonsingular limiting Hessian \(-\lambda I/4\); its applicability to the lexicographically selected global maximizer, rather than merely to a stationary point, is exactly the global-localization content required of the stated joint-system proviso.

Let \(\rho_j=\rho_j(\kappa,\gamma,\lambda,R)\) denote the deterministic selected-norm limit delivered by that same proviso.  The reverse triangle inequality, the preceding two displays, and convergence of \(\|\widehat\beta_{jn}\|_2\) to \(\rho_j\) give
\[
 \rho_j^2
 =\frac{16}{\lambda^2}s_j\kappa+o(\kappa),
 \qquad j\in\mathcal J.
\]
Indeed, the second display gives \(\|\widehat\beta_{jn}\|_2=(4/\lambda)\|G_{jn}\|_2+o_{\mathbb P}(\sqrt\kappa)\), and squaring is legitimate because the first display makes both leading norms \(O_{\mathbb P}(\sqrt\kappa)\).  Since \(R>0\) is fixed, \(\rho_j=O(\sqrt\kappa)<R\) for all sufficiently small positive \(\kappa\).  Thus the radius constraint is inactive in this reduction.

It remains to convert norm into population regret.  Proposition \(\mathrm{prop{:}radial\mbox{-}invariance}\) gives \(g(0)=0\),
\[
 g'(r)=r\,\mathbb E\!\left[Z^2\sigma'(rZ)\right],
\]
and \(0<\sigma'(x)\le 1/4\).  Since \(\mathbb E Z^2=1\), dominated convergence gives
\[
 \lim_{r\downarrow0}\frac{g'(r)}r=\frac14.
\]
Integrating this expansion from \(0\) to \(r\) yields
\[
 g(r)=\frac{r^2}{8}+o(r^2)
 \qquad (r\downarrow0).
\]
By the radial-regret identity in Proposition \(\mathrm{prop{:}radial\mbox{-}invariance}\) and the definition \(r_j=\lambda g(\rho_j)\),
\[
 r_j
 =\frac{\lambda}{8}\rho_j^2+o(\kappa)
 =\frac{2s_j}{\lambda}\kappa+o(\kappa).
\]
Substitution of \(s_T=1/8\), \(s_E=1/16\), and \(s_D=v_\gamma/4\) proves
\[
 r_T=\frac{\kappa}{4\lambda}+o(\kappa),
 \qquad
 r_E=\frac{\kappa}{8\lambda}+o(\kappa),
 \qquad
 r_D=\frac{v_\gamma\kappa}{2\lambda}+o(\kappa).
\]
Finally, because \(\gamma\ge\underline\gamma>0\), one has
\[
 \sigma(\gamma Z)\{1-\sigma(\gamma Z)\}\le\frac14
\]
with strict inequality almost surely, since a standard normal variable is nonzero almost surely.  Hence \(v_\gamma<1/4\), so \(s_D<s_E\): exact same-coordinate linear balance gives only a partial efficient-score projection.  This comparison is ancillary to, and consistent with, the three claimed expansions.
